patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Adapt.io and Clay share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Adapt.io only if your buying job matches “Regional B2B contact database with credit plans — Free; Starter $49/mo; Basic $99/mo; Cust” rather than Clay's shape. Choose Clay only if your buying job matches “GTM data enrichment and workflow platform for multi-provider waterfall prospecting — Free ” rather than Adapt.io's shape. Workflow advantage: Adapt.io leans contact-management; Clay leans lead-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Adapt.io and Clay share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Adapt.io is Regional B2B contact database with credit plans — Free; Starter $49/mo; Basic $99/mo; Custom contact sales; 7-day trial.; Clay is GTM data enrichment and workflow platform for multi-provider waterfall prospecting — Free + Launch from ~$167/mo headline, Growth, Enterpris.
- Company-size focus: Adapt.io (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Clay (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Adapt.io-leaning contact-management vs Clay-leaning lead-management.
- Researched limits: Adapt.io — Thinner global mega-database depth than UpLead/Hunter/Apollo-class peers for many buyer niches; Clay — Learning curve is steep for non-technical GTM users — table/waterfall mental model.

Limitations — Adapt.io: Thinner global mega-database depth than UpLead/Hunter/Apollo-class peers for many buyer niches; No native email sequencing — data/export first; Clay: Learning curve is steep for non-technical GTM users — table/waterfall mental model; Credit consumption across providers requires ongoing cost governance.

Poor-fit cases: Adapt.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Thinner global mega-database depth than UpLead/Hunter/Apollo-class peers for many buyer niches · Clay is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Learning curve is steep for non-technical GTM users — table/waterfall mental model · Avoid Adapt.io if you actually need Clay's motion (GTM data enrichment and workflow platform for multi-provider waterfall prospecti)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
